links.note: English adds “who were” to express the Greek attributive construction.
English identifies the otherwise unnamed heart as Judas’s.
English names the subject of the Greek participle.
Greek says the Father gave things “to him,” identifying whose hands receive them.
Greek “girded himself” describes wrapping the towel around his waist.
The participle describes being girded with the towel.
English uses a possessive where Greek has the article.
English repeats the plural pronoun after “all.”
English makes putting the garments back on explicit with the Greek verb “took.”
English supplies the predicate after Greek “I am.”
The participle describes reclining at a meal.
English expresses the dipping as a time clause preceding the giving.
